correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is an interior lower Nisqually River reach beside the southern Nisqually Reservation, not the natural headwater. Direct Nisqually River labels identify the adjacent active river. The first small northward elbow touches the northern valley-edge slope before returning toward the river; the remainder crosses the broad connected wooded floodplain and meander setting. This supports ordinary river-valley and valley-margin correspondence, without claiming that every stored position lies on the contemporary channel or flat valley floor.

The second part continues northwest through the same lower Nisqually valley. It crosses the large meander and side-channel/wetland floor, touches the western channel margin, and returns toward the eastern valley side. Repeated direct Nisqually River labels establish the selected receiving mainstem. The original shared join with the first part and the northern join with the third part remain within this continuous river-valley setting; no separate tributary is substituted for the mainstem.

The third part takes a long generalized northwest chord along the Nisqually valley and valley-margin corridor past the Nisqually settlement and across Interstate 5, then continues through the lower estuarine marsh and turns northeast across the river-mouth floor. The line cuts meanders, floodplain interiors and short valley-edge ground rather than following the exact mapped bank. The named Nisqually River remains the connected receiving river throughout. The terminal eastward segment crosses the marsh beside the main tidal channel, north of the Red Salmon Creek wetland setting.

correspondence.component_scope: river mouth and tidal flat ending
correspondence.finding: The fourth part continues northeast and then north across the Nisqually mouth marsh and the intertidal-flat setting directly adjacent to its terminal channel. Nisqually Flats is directly mapped as the receiving flat component. The source endpoint lies slightly farther north than the rendered endpoint; both fall within this northern mouth/intertidal-flat setting. The quantized stored final position remains separate from the higher-precision render endpoint. No surveyed mouth line, exact distributary, continuously wet thread or present bank is asserted.

findings.part_basis: Original fragment and part indices are zero-based; every stated span is inclusive. FID 9456, logical FID 3034, is the single stage 3 mainstem fragment: local and aggregate parts 0–3, one-based 1–4. Their position counts are 8, 5, 5 and 3, totaling 21 stored positions including repeated part endpoints. Within-part position spans are stated separately. Original order, role, stage, every part and all three original part joins are preserved. No joining, reversal, simplification, repair or source-geometry reconstruction. Source endpoint, higher-precision render endpoint and quantized stored ending remain distinct.

terminal_observations.source_endpoint: Separately located slightly farther north in the mapped Nisqually mouth/intertidal-flat setting.
terminal_observations.render_endpoint: Separately located slightly south and east of the source endpoint in the same mouth/intertidal-flat setting, adjoining the terminal channel.
terminal_observations.stored_final_coordinate: Separately retained quantized final position in the render-ending setting; not substituted for the higher-precision render endpoint.
terminal_observations.geographic_interpretation: The final selected passage crosses the river-mouth marsh toward the adjacent intertidal flats. Stored sea metadata is retained but does not prove that either endpoint is continuously water-covered or marks an exact river mouth.
terminal_observations.limit: No exact distributary, modern bank, tide state or surveyed mouth vertex is inferred; the source and render endings are not conflated.

uncertainties: The Nisqually River candidate is a bounded representative system identity only; accepted, scalar and Korean names remain null, with no product application.

The generalized stored line sometimes touches valley-edge slopes and crosses floodplain or marsh interiors. Ordinary connected corridor correspondence does not establish exact current channel alignment.
Both distinct endpoints lie in the mouth/intertidal-flat setting. Their present wetness, exact relationship to the bank and surveyed mouth status are unverified.
Individual source-map epochs, current flow/tidal conditions, legal naming extent and formal registry status remain unverified.

correspondence.finding: The three-position opening descends south from the lower river through a wooded and cultivated alluvial corridor, then turns southwest. The actual channel meanders beside the straight selected segments; all lie in the same connected lower-river floor.

The second original part continues south and southwest around the same river bend into the lower floodplain. Its short generalized segments cross channel margins without requiring a separate connecting river or land-divide crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: westward lower river and estuarine widening
correspondence.finding: The five-position third part turns west and then northwest through the broadening river, adjoining swamp/mangrove floor and agricultural edge. The original image shows an unbroken river corridor through every selected turn and both adjoining part joins.

correspondence.finding: The last part follows the broad lower bend westward toward the estuarine entrance. Straight segments cut mangrove-island and channel-edge interiors in the connected mouth complex. The source ending is in estuarine water; the separate render and stored endings are on the wooded northern bank fringe. The selected line ends there rather than continuing into the open gulf.

correspondence.finding: The opening two-position part runs east across the low-lying wetland and partly open vegetation south of the named lower river. The map places it in the same coastal floodplain beside small drainage lines. It is a selected starting position, not an identified natural headwater or a separately named river.

This five-position part first continues east, then cuts northeast across wetland and a wooded floodplain belt before turning north and northeast toward the broad river’s western margin. It crosses a visible narrow side channel that enters the main river farther east. The original map also depicts small drainage in this lowland. The diagonal is retained as a generalized floodplain approach, not asserted to follow that side channel or an exact continuous wet thread. There is no observed intervening ridge or separate closed basin requiring a hypothetical interbasin link.

The short eastward part passes from the wooded western bank fringe into the ordinary lower-river corridor. The direct Rio Amapá Grande label is on this receiving trunk in the original municipal map. Scattered cloud and shadow in the imagery do not supply a new channel claim; the original map and visible surrounding river corridor together establish the broad bank-to-river setting.

The three-position part turns southeast along the broad Rio Amapá Grande corridor, then east through the lower joining reach. Its straight segment is generalized across the river and its bank fringe. The separately mapped Rio Flechal arrives from the south near the downstream end; that incoming southern river remains a distinct component, not an alternative name for the selected trunk.

The two-position part heads northeast through the broad confluence and bend setting, cutting the wooded inner-bank corner before re-entering open river. The whole shortcut remains within one connected river and alluvial-margin setting; no exact-bank, current-flow or straight wet-channel equivalence is claimed.

This four-position part turns north, northeast and east around the western and northern side of the lowland enclosed by the river branches. Both the map and imagery show the continuous broad river bend. The final position is the unchanged shared join with the stage 2 mainstem fragment.

The second fragment’s first two-position part continues east across the broad northern river bend, north of the mapped Ilha do Meio reference locality. The stage 3/stage 2 transition lies within the same connected lower-river corridor.

The final three-position part turns southeast through the broad river bend and then northeast toward its northern bank fringe. The separately retained source endpoint lies in broad river water southeast of the render ending. The higher-precision render endpoint and quantized stored ending reach the same ordinary northern shoreline/fringe setting. The map continues the named river east toward the Atlantic beyond this endpoint; the stored sea class is retained without moving the endpoint to the coast.

findings.part_basis: Original fragment and within-fragment part indices are zero-based; every span is inclusive. Mainstem FID11620/logical FID3398 is fragment 0 of 2, stage 3, local parts 0–5 (one-based 1–6), aggregate parts 0–5 (one-based 1–6), with respectively 2,5,2,3,2,4 stored positions. Mainstem FID11621/logical FID3398 is fragment 1 of 2, stage 2, local parts 0–1 (one-based 1–2), aggregate parts 6–7 (one-based 7–8), with respectively 2,3 positions. All 8 parts and 23 positions retain their original order. Within-part position spans are explicit. No joining, reversal, simplification, repair, source-geometry reconstruction or natural-headwater inference. Source endpoint, higher-precision render endpoint and quantized stored ending remain distinct.

Map compilation dates and imagery scene dates differ and do not establish present bank positions, tide or continuous flow.
Scattered image clouds and shadows prevent claims about every surface pixel; the original municipal map supplies complementary ordinary geographic correspondence.

correspondence.finding: The northern four-position opening descends beside a wooded river bend in a cultivated alluvial plain. The western wetland and eastern fields frame one connected river corridor; the stored straight line cuts meander margins rather than precisely following the photographed channel.

The second part continues south and southwest within the same river and floodplain belt. A minor adjacent eastern channel and field drains are not treated as the selected river identity or as a required alternative link.
This short two-position part remains on the eastern margin of the broad river corridor. Its join to the next part is on the same connected alluvial floor, not a separate basin transfer.

The fourth original part continues south across the cultivated eastern river-margin floor while the photographed channel curves to its west. This is ordinary continuous alluvial-corridor correspondence; the straight stored segment is not a claimed present wet channel.

The fifth part approaches and crosses the eastern side of the prominent lower meander. Its straight chords pass through fields and wooded banks, but the original image establishes the enclosing continuous river bend and floodplain.
The sixth part cuts southwest across the wooded inside of the lower meander within the same connected river floor. It does not establish a short artificial watercourse across that interior.
The seventh part continues southwest through the lower river and riparian strip as the channel straightens toward the receiving estuary.

The eighth part follows the lower southwestward river reach, with wetland to the west and vegetated upland margin to the east. The final bend leads continuously toward the larger receiving river visible downstream.
